cards.title: Competitor review research for purchase objections
cards.claim: Spending 30–60 minutes reading competitor reviews and other sources (Trustpilot, BBB, Facebook ad comments, Instagram followers, Facebook Ad Library) can help identify potential objections that prevent customers from buying.
cards.action: Spend at least 30 minutes to an hour reviewing competitor reviews and list as many possible competitor objections as you can; also check Trustpilot, BBB, Facebook ad comments, view 50–75 Instagram followers of a niche competitor, and search Facebook Ad Library for problem key phrases.
applies_when: You are preparing to write ecommerce email copy and need to understand purchase barriers.
unknowns: How to handle privacy when viewing follower profiles.
evidence_quotes: troll through these reviews for like at least 30 minutes to an hour list out as many possible competitor objections as you can so that way you can understand all of the potential things that would prevent someone from buying from you
you can also take a look at like trust pilot Better Business Bureau all of these things to find even more reviews to delve deeper
you can also look into the comment sections of their Facebook ads
maybe check between 50 to like 75 people
you type in hair loss on Facebook ad library and see what products and solutions are already available on the market when it comes to hair loss

cards.title: Modular email copy blocks
cards.claim: Ecommerce email copy can be assembled from modular blocks: banner, CTA, review, product display, benefit highlight, content/story, countdown timers, featured on, and guarantees.
cards.action: Write copy for individual blocks (banner, CTA, review, product display, benefit highlight, content/story, countdown timers, featured on, guarantees) and assemble the email by arranging these blocks.
applies_when: You are building or writing ecommerce email marketing copy.
unknowns: Exact copy requirements for each block are not detailed.
Whether all blocks are needed in every email.
evidence_quotes: in terms of all possible blocks it's going to be your banner block your CTA block review blocks product display blocks benefit highlight blocks content or story type of blocks
if you know how to write copy for all of these Blocks individually building out an email becomes a lot easier
you can have like countdown timers and featured on for like Authority and brand building to ensure trust you can also write guarantees

cards.title: Review block objection handling
cards.claim: Generic positive reviews ('I love this product') do not help customers decide; strategically selected reviews that address core objections are more useful.
cards.action: Select reviews that mention the core objections and problems of your audience; consider pairing with UGC, but avoid tying a reviewer's face to sensitive objections such as erectile dysfunction.
applies_when: You are adding a review block to an ecommerce email.
do_not_use_when: The objection is sensitive and using UGC could expose the reviewer's identity.
unknowns: How to obtain consent for UGC.
How to verify reviews handle objections effectively.
evidence_quotes: most people when it comes to putting reviews into their emails they don't actually strategically select the reviews to handle objections
I love this product doesn't actually help the customer to make a decision on whether or not to try this product or not
you want to pick reviews that handle the objections for you
you want to pick the reviews that mention the core objections and the core problems that your audience might have
if someone left a review about like erectile dysfunction obviously you don't want to put their face next to it
